OL26320A.name: J. R. R. Tolkien
OL26320A.bio: English writer, poet, and philologist, best known for The Hobbit and The Lord of the Rings. He was the Rawlinson and Bosworth Professor of Anglo-Saxon at Oxford.

OL118077A.name: George Orwell
OL118077A.bio: English novelist, essayist, journalist, and critic known for the allegorical novella Animal Farm and the dystopian novel Nineteen Eighty-Four.

OL27460A.name: Jane Austen
OL27460A.bio: English novelist whose works of romantic fiction set among the landed gentry earned her a place as one of the most widely read writers in English literature.

OL23919A.name: Charles Dickens
OL23919A.bio: English writer and social critic regarded as the greatest novelist of the Victorian era, creator of A Christmas Carol, Great Expectations, and Oliver Twist.

OL1055597A.name: Ernest Hemingway
OL1055597A.bio: American novelist, short-story writer, and journalist known for A Farewell to Arms and The Old Man and the Sea; Nobel Prize laureate in Literature in 1954.

OL40757A.name: F. Scott Fitzgerald
OL40757A.bio: American novelist and short-story writer of the Jazz Age, best known for The Great Gatsby.

OL21594A.name: Herman Melville
OL21594A.bio: American novelist, short story writer, and poet of the American Renaissance, best known for Moby-Dick.

OL31569A.name: Leo Tolstoy
OL31569A.bio: Russian writer regarded as one of the greatest authors of all time; received nominations for the Nobel Prize in Literature and the Nobel Peace Prize.

OL22225A.name: Fyodor Dostoevsky
OL22225A.bio: Russian novelist, short story writer, essayist, and journalist whose works explore human psychology in the troubled political, social, and spiritual atmospheres of 19th-century Russia.

OL18319A.name: Mark Twain
OL18319A.bio: American writer, humorist, entrepreneur, publisher, and lecturer, hailed as the greatest humorist the United States has produced.

OL22088A.name: Charlotte Bronte
OL22088A.bio: English novelist and poet, the eldest of the three Bronte sisters who survived into adulthood, whose novel Jane Eyre is an English literature classic.

OL34384A.name: Isaac Asimov
OL34384A.bio: American writer and professor of biochemistry, known for his works of science fiction and popular science, including the Foundation and Robot series.

OL220519A.name: Arthur C. Clarke
OL220519A.bio: British science fiction writer, science writer, and futurist, inventor, undersea explorer, and co-writer of the screenplay for 2001: A Space Odyssey.

OL22138A.name: Ursula K. Le Guin
OL22138A.bio: American author best known for her works of speculative fiction, including the Earthsea fantasy series and The Left Hand of Darkness.

OL533229A.name: Terry Pratchett
OL533229A.bio: English humorist, satirist, and author of fantasy novels, best known for the Discworld series of 41 novels.

OL390776A.name: Neil Gaiman
OL390776A.bio: English author of short fiction, novels, comic books, graphic novels, audio theatre, and films, known for American Gods and The Sandman.

OL27082A.name: George R. R. Martin
OL27082A.bio: American novelist, screenwriter, television producer, and short story writer, best known for the series of epic fantasy novels A Song of Ice and Fire.

OL23919AR.name: J. K. Rowling
OL23919AR.bio: British author and philanthropist, best known for writing the Harry Potter fantasy series, which has sold over 600 million copies.

OL27294A.name: Douglas Adams
OL27294A.bio: English author, screenwriter, essayist, humorist, satirist and dramatist, best known for The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy.

OL40976A.name: Ray Bradbury
OL40976A.bio: American author and screenwriter, one of the most celebrated 20th-century American writers, known for Fahrenheit 451 and The Martian Chronicles.

OL19377A.name: Aldous Huxley
OL19377A.bio: English writer and philosopher, author of nearly fifty books, including the dystopian novel Brave New World.

OL52939A.name: Margaret Atwood
OL52939A.bio: Canadian poet, novelist, literary critic, essayist, teacher, environmental activist, and inventor, best known for The Handmaid's Tale.

OL39084A.name: Toni Morrison
OL39084A.bio: American novelist, essayist, book editor, and college professor whose first novel The Bluest Eye was published in 1970; Nobel Prize laureate in Literature in 1993.

OL241047A.name: Haruki Murakami
OL241047A.bio: Japanese writer whose novels, essays, and short stories have been bestsellers in Japan and internationally, with his work translated into 50 languages.

OL43525A.name: Gabriel Garcia Marquez
OL43525A.bio: Colombian novelist, short-story writer, screenwriter and journalist, known affectionately as Gabo throughout Latin America; Nobel Prize laureate in Literature in 1982.

OL19270A.name: J. D. Salinger
OL19270A.bio: American writer best known for his 1951 novel The Catcher in the Rye, whose reclusive later life made him a subject of fascination.

OL21781A.name: Kurt Vonnegut
OL21781A.bio: American writer known for his satirical and darkly humorous novels, including Slaughterhouse-Five and Cat's Cradle.

OL17881A.name: Harper Lee
OL17881A.bio: American novelist whose 1960 novel To Kill a Mockingbird won the 1961 Pulitzer Prize and became a classic of modern American literature.

OL2623822A.name: Yuval Noah Harari
OL2623822A.bio: Israeli medievalist, military historian, public intellectual, and writer, professor at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem, author of Sapiens.

OL11578A.name: Stephen Hawking
OL11578A.bio: English theoretical physicist, cosmologist, and author, director of research at the Centre for Theoretical Cosmology at the University of Cambridge.

OL54935A.name: Daniel Kahneman
OL54935A.bio: Israeli-American psychologist and economist notable for his work on the psychology of judgment and decision-making; awarded the 2002 Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences.

OL22433A.name: Rachel Carson
OL22433A.bio: American marine biologist, writer, and conservationist whose writings are credited with advancing the global environmental movement.

OL22129A.name: Charles Darwin
OL22129A.bio: English naturalist, geologist, and biologist, widely known for his contributions to evolutionary biology, especially On the Origin of Species.

OL22037A.name: Maurice Sendak
OL22037A.bio: American illustrator and writer of children's books, best known for Where the Wild Things Are, first published in 1963.

OL22807A.name: E. B. White
OL22807A.bio: American writer, best known for his children's books Charlotte's Web and Stuart Little, and for his work as a writer and contributor to The New Yorker.

OL2695761A.name: Dr. Seuss
OL2695761A.bio: American children's author, political cartoonist, illustrator, poet, animator, and filmmaker, known for The Cat in the Hat and Green Eggs and Ham.

OL22950A.name: Roald Dahl
OL22950A.bio: British novelist, short-story writer, poet, screenwriter, and wartime fighter pilot, his books have sold more than 250 million copies worldwide.

OL21594AL.name: Lewis Carroll
OL21594AL.bio: English writer, mathematician, logician, Anglican deacon, and photographer, best known for Alice's Adventures in Wonderland and Through the Looking-Glass.

OL16857A.name: Robert Frost
OL16857A.bio: American poet, known for his realistic depictions of rural life and his command of American colloquial speech, frequently honored during his lifetime.

OL19169A.name: Sylvia Plath
OL19169A.bio: American poet, novelist, and short-story writer, credited with advancing the genre of confessional poetry, best known for The Bell Jar.
